answer: The inlet multiplier is published, charged in beacon, and karst lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3424 identities would post 4416 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
